one_liner: MPFR 4.2.1 with a CUDA/CGBN backend: bit-identical batched mul/div/sqrt/fma, 18-30x over one CPU core, 115-284x device-resident.
what_it_does: A full GNU MPFR 4.2.1 tree that, when configured with --enable-cgbn, adds a header <mpfr-cgbn.h> with batch functions over contiguous mpfr_t arrays (mpfr_cgbn_mul/sqr/add/sub/div/sqrt/fma), device-resident vectors (mpfr_cgbn_vec_*), and an off-by-default hook that diverts scalar mpfr_mul/sqr/div/sqrt/fma calls to the GPU. Every result is meant to match scalar MPFR exactly: same correctly rounded value, ternary value and flags in all five rounding modes, checked by tests/tcgbn. Without --enable-cgbn the library is stock MPFR with no new exported symbols, so existing code keeps working and only new call sites get the speedup.
how_it_is_fast: Significands are packed left-aligned into fixed-width CGBN integers (a ladder of 13 widths from 128 to 65536 bits) and each element is computed by a cooperative group of 4-32 GPU threads per instance, so thousands of independent operations run in parallel. The kernels form the exact (2x or, for fma, 3x width) result with CGBN integer arithmetic and round it on the device; exponent range and flags are applied back on the host. Batches are staged through page-locked buffers in chunks of up to 32 MiB, and device-resident vectors skip the PCIe round trip entirely, which is where the 100x-plus factors come from.
when_to_use: Many independent MPFR operations of one precision between 4096 and 16384 bits, in batches of a few thousand: the README calls this the sweet spot (resident mul 230x at 4096 bits, div 157x at 16384, n = 16384).
Chains of operations that can stay on the GPU (vec_mul, vec_fma, vec_div ... then one vec_get): resident fma reaches 284x at 8192 bits.
One-shot batches of about 1024 or more mul, div, sqrt or fma at 2048-32768 bits where data must round-trip each call: batch div 30.4x and sqrt 28.2x at 32768 bits, mul 4.9x at 4096 bits (n = 1024).
Code that must keep MPFR's exact semantics (rounding modes, ternary values, exception flags) while moving bulk arithmetic to an NVIDIA GPU.
when_not_to_use: Single operations or small batches: n = 1 is always slower (launch floor about 6.5 us resident, 16 us with transfers), and batch mul at 128-512 bits stays at or below 1.8x even at n = 16384.
Batched addition or subtraction with transfers: every add batch cell is 0.7x or less; add only pays on resident data between other operations.

Division or square root above 32768 bits: CGBN switches to a much slower algorithm (div 71x, sqrt 163x slower per instance from 32768 to 40960 bits) and the backend still sends them to the GPU, where they lose to the CPU.
Precision above 65536 bits, transcendental functions (exp, log, sin and others are not offloaded), batches with mixed result precisions, or hosts without an NVIDIA GPU and CUDA.
When you can spread scalar MPFR over many CPU cores: all ratios are against one core, so a 16-core run at linear scaling would cut the 18-30x batch peaks to about 1-2x (derived from page data).

integration.dependencies: GMP 5.0.0+ with GMP_NUMB_BITS a multiple of 32, CUDA toolkit with nvcc (developed against 13.2) and libcudart, the header-only CGBN tree (README links the author's fork steleman/nvidia-cgbn), libstdc++, pthreads (optional, for the device mutex)
integration.min_toolchain: nvcc from CUDA 13.2 as tested (older toolkits not documented); host GCC 14.3.1 in the design PDF; GPU compute capability 3.5 or later
integration.platforms: NVIDIA GPUs only (sm_35+; tested on an RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell, sm_120); build instructions are Linux/autotools (gmake), other OSes not documented; static and shared libmpfr both supported
integration.thread_safety: Concurrent calls from several threads are safe but serialized on one internal mutex when pthread.h is found at configure time (no lock otherwise); MPFR's flags and exponent range stay thread-local, but the auto-offload threshold is a plain process-wide global
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — it is ABI-compatible libmpfr and existing scalar code is unchanged, but speedups need the new mpfr_cgbn_* batch or vector calls; the transparent scalar hook works but is slower (e.g. 1024-bit mul 0.18 us off vs 17.8 us on)

gotchas: Cost follows the width rung, not the precision asked for: a 33000-bit operand does 40960-bit work, and one bit above 40960 moves it to 49152.
If the result elements in a batch do not all share one precision, or it exceeds 65536 bits, the call silently runs on the CPU; the return value (elements done on the device) is the only signal.
Device-vector arithmetic runs in MPFR's extended exponent range; emin/emax checks and exception flags only happen in mpfr_cgbn_vec_get.
Widths above 32768 bits use CGBN beyond its documented maximum (checked against GMP by tests/cgbn-verify); MPFR_RNDF is evaluated as MPFR_RNDZ with a meaningless ternary value.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick this over raw CGBN or midint-arithmetic-division when you need correctly rounded MPFR floating point (all rounding modes, flags) rather than fixed-width integers, and over APFP when the hardware is an NVIDIA GPU rather than an FPGA and the work is element-wise batches rather than 512-bit matrix multiply.
verified_claims_summary: First-party wall-clock measurements (tests/cgbnbench) on an NVIDIA RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell with CUDA 13.2, MPFR 4.2.1, GMP 6.3.0 and GCC 14.3.1, against scalar MPFR in a loop on one core of an unnamed CPU in the same machine: batch peaks of 18-30x at n = 1024 (div 30.4x, sqrt 28.2x at 32768 bits) and resident peaks of 115-284x at n = 16384 (fma 284x at 8192 bits). Host CFLAGS and the CPU model are not stated, and a multi-core MPFR baseline was not measured.
status_note: One 'Initial Github commit' on 2026-09-12 (3 stars, 0 forks, 0 issues) with a detailed README, design PDF and correctness tests; LGPL-3.0-or-later sources inside a stock MPFR 4.2.1 tree, so it is usable, but it is a personal fork with no upstream MPFR release carrying it found.
